line: HP OmniBook X Flip 14 (2025, AMD Ryzen AI) — Spectre x360 14 successor
config_name: OmniBook X Flip 14 — Ryzen AI 7 450, 32GB LPDDR5x, 1TB SSD, 2K OLED touch

battery.notes: Strix Point draws more than Lunar/Panther Lake in light use; OLED penalty included. Estimate.

price.notes: VERIFIED BBY 19817319 at $2,499.99 (no discount). Poor value vs Panther Lake twin at $2,179.

offers.name: HP OmniBook X Flip 14" 2K OLED Touchscreen Copilot+ PC Laptop - AMD Ryzen Ai7 450 - 32GB LPDDR5X - 1TB SSD - Windows 11 Home - AMD Radeon 860M Graphics - Deep Espresso Aluminum

reviews.quote: Flexible performance with AMD Zen 5. Pros: portable and travel-friendly USB-C AC adapter, strong CPU performance for the size, full sRGB colors at minimum, integrated HDMI and USB-A, strong chassis design, great battery life. Cons: HDR only available on highest-end SKU, no Arc B390 or Radeon 890M options, 1200p OLED panel could be brighter, new keyboard takes getting used to. (NBC review of the OmniBook X Flip 14 AMD Zen 5 config.)

praises: 32GB RAM — double the Intel twins, better for heavy multitasking
Radeon 860M is the strongest iGPU here: light 1080p gaming actually works
2K OLED panel is vivid with perfect blacks
Strong Zen 5 multicore for short bursts
Deep Espresso aluminum finish is the nicest of the line
complaints: BBY owners rate it only 2.82/5 across 17 reviews — by far the worst of the line
Reports of sleep/wake failures, driver instability, and fan weirdness on the AMD build (drives the 2.8-star score)
Noticeably worse battery life than the Intel Panther Lake twin in the same chassis
No Thunderbolt (USB4 only) and fewer docking guarantees
$2,500 with no discount while the Intel OLED tier sells for $2,179

design_philosophy: The AMD Strix Point variant of HP's premium convertible was meant to offer the stronger iGPU and 32GB for creators on a budget, but in Canada it became the line's black sheep: same chassis as the well-liked Intel model, visibly worse customer satisfaction (2.82 stars vs 4.14), and no price advantage.
rating_notes: Pro score attached from NBC review of the OmniBook X Flip 14 AMD Zen 5 config (86%, gap-fill 2026-11-24). Inferred from Intel OmniBook X Flip 14 sibling (entry 30): +1.5 gaming / +1 productivity for 860M+32GB, -1 battery / -1.5 thermals_noise for Strix Point in a thin convertible, per BBY user reports (2.82★/17 — worst-rated CA OmniBook listing we found; treat reliability complaints as load-bearing). Durability docked for that instability signal. No pro review of this exact config found (bot-walls — see SHARED-hp-convertibles.md). Image URL from BBY 16" AMD twin (this SKU's image field was null).
dealbreakers: Worse battery than Intel twin at higher price
